The video features a close-up view of a sink drain with a stopper. A man can be seen working on it, tightening the bolts, and turning the stopper counterclockwise. The sink drain is filled with water and then the water is draining through the stopper. The sink is filled with water and is turned off and on by the man. Another person also attempts to fix the sink, and a little girl is watching.
The video is taken indoors. The sink has lots of pipes under the sink, and water is running from them. They appear to be fixing the sink drain so the water goes down the drain properly. The man is tightening the bolts to ensure the water goes down the drain without any problems.

summary.brief: A man shows how to remove, clean, and reinstall a bathroom sink stopper to clear a clog.
summary.detailed: The video begins with the presenter pointing out a clogged bathroom sink and turning off the water. He examines the stopper from above, finds it attached to a rod, and decides to work from underneath. After removing a cover plate and unscrewing a small nut, he pulls the stopper out, exposing a rubber ball and debris. He wipes away the mess with a towel, repositions the ball, and threads the stopper back into place, tightening the nut and other bolts with a wrench. He then runs water to test drainage, shines a flashlight into the pipe to check for leaks, and confirms the sink drains properly. A young child watches nearby, and the video ends with a thank‑you graphic.

action.detailed: Unscrew the cover plate, pull out the stopper, clean out debris and the rubber ball, reinsert and tighten the stopper and related bolts, run water to test flow, and use a flashlight to inspect for leaks.
action.actor: A man (the video presenter) working on the bathroom sink

summary.brief: A hand removes the pop‑up stopper, loosens the nearby pipe fittings, cleans the area, and then reassembles the stopper and fittings.
summary.detailed: The video opens with the presenter greeting the audience and explaining that the bathroom sink is clogged. He examines the pop‑up stopper from above, noting that the top cover is attached to a rod and cannot be pulled straight out. The camera then moves under the sink where a silver pipe and a blue pipe with handles are visible. Using a flashlight and a wrench, he unscrews the silver nut, removes a metal screen from a rod, and also unscrews the top of the blue pipe and removes its handle. He pulls the metal stopper (a white ball‑type plug) out of the drain and places a towel beneath the sink in case water drips. After cleaning the area, he positions the stopper back over the drain opening, slides the rod back into place, and screws the cover back on, tightening the nuts with the wrench. He checks that water can flow freely and confirms there are no leaks, concluding with a brief “great job.” The gray carpet‑like floor and the brown cabinet above the sink are visible throughout.
